Class BehaviorKeys

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.window.BehaviorKeys
public final class BehaviorKeys extends Object
The library's built-in BehaviorKeys. The engine is generic, so this set grows one constant at a time as each behavior's phase lands — adding a behavior is adding a key here (or, for a server-tier behavior whose value type is an MKC type, an equivalent constant MKC-side).

Phase 3a defines the client-tier keys whose value types are simple and known now — enough to exercise the engine MK-alone. Phase 4 adds the reactive verbs: their value type (ReactiveHook) is an MK type, so all four reaction keys live here — the SERVER-tier ON_INSERT/ON_TAKE and the CLIENT-tier observed variants — letting an MK-alone consumer name even the server verbs (only the firing of the server ones requires MKC). Still owed (added with their phases, by value type):

  • client-tier, complex value: DECORATION, HOVER, ON_CLICK, PARITY (Phase 5/6).
  • server-tier whose value type is an MKC type (so MKC-side in MKCBehaviorKeys): GATING, QUICK_MOVE, DROP_RULE, BINDING, MENDING.

  • Field Details

    • VISIBILITY

      public static final BehaviorKey<VisibilityRule> VISIBILITY
      Whether an addressable thing is shown — a client-side VisibilityRule predicate (re-evaluated each frame), so one key spans static hide and dynamic reveal (hover). Client-tier, every kind. Default VisibilityRule.VISIBLE. Resolved + evaluated on the client only (never server-side; see VisibilityRule).

    • OPACITY

      public static final BehaviorKey<TriBool> OPACITY
      Whether a panel is interaction-opaque (eats clicks over its bounds). Client- tier, panels only. Default TriBool.TRUE (M9: panels opaque by default).

    • INERTNESS

      public static final BehaviorKey<TriBool> INERTNESS
      Whether a panel makes what it covers inert. Client-tier, panels only. Default TriBool.FALSE (a panel is not inert-making unless declared).

    • ON_INSERT

      public static final BehaviorKey<ReactiveHook> ON_INSERT
      Fires when a slot gains content, on the server inside the menu transaction (authoritative; may have game-state effects). SERVER tier → fires only with MKC present (the firing seams are the architecture's named owed gap). Default ReactiveHook.NONE.

    • ON_TAKE

      public static final BehaviorKey<ReactiveHook> ON_TAKE
      Fires when a slot loses content, on the server inside the menu transaction. SERVER tier; default ReactiveHook.NONE.

    • ON_INSERT_OBSERVED

      public static final BehaviorKey<ReactiveHook> ON_INSERT_OBSERVED
      Fires on the client when synced slot contents grow — pure UI feedback (flash, sound, badge), no authority. CLIENT tier → MK-alone capable, and fires for created slots too (their contents sync identically). Default ReactiveHook.NONE.

    • ON_TAKE_OBSERVED

      public static final BehaviorKey<ReactiveHook> ON_TAKE_OBSERVED
      Fires on the client when synced slot contents shrink — pure UI feedback, no authority. CLIENT tier; default ReactiveHook.NONE.
